source.source_date_epoch_provenance: the time release 2.4.71-CE-ubuntu24.04-r5 was cut (2026-11-25T22:05:06Z), by scripts/rerelease-agenda.py: ReadyStack dates an image by when its release was packaged (owner 2026-11-10), recorded here once and used by every rebuild of the release; it builds upstream commit 4554c7436049, dated 2026-11-09T03:07:05Z (source.commit_epoch).
source._build_note: The git tag has no configure script: buildconf makes it in the vendor stage from Ubuntu's APR build files (/usr/share/apr-1.0/build, libapr1-dev), which do not include config.guess and config.sub, so they are copied from autotools-dev; python3 is buildconf's own requirement. The offline build runs ./configure, make and make install into /opt/httpd against the system APR (apr-1-config, apu-1-config). Measured 2026-11-08 on ubuntu:24.04: buildconf, configure, make and make install in about 70 s; `httpd -V` reports Apache/2.4.70 (Unix), APR 1.7.2, APR-UTIL 1.6.3, PCRE 10.42, event MPM; 96 modules. The manual (42 MB of HTML) and the man pages are not shipped. gcc honours SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, so `httpd -V`'s "Server built" line is the source date. --disable-ldap --disable-authnz-ldap (r2, 2026-11-09): `most` built mod_ldap and mod_authnz_ldap because Ubuntu's APR-util has LDAP support, but they load libldap and liblber, which r1 never installed (`ldd` on 2.4.70-r1: libldap.so.2 => not found), so neither could be loaded there; the chiselled runtime's library check refuses a module whose library the rootfs lacks, and OpenLDAP's client library would bring GnuTLS and Cyrus SASL for two modules nobody could use.

rootfs_run: sed -i -e 's/^Listen 80$/Listen 8080/' -e 's/^User daemon$/User httpd/' -e 's/^Group daemon$/Group httpd/' -e 's/^ServerAdmin you@example.com$/ServerAdmin webmaster@localhost/' -e 's/^#ServerName www.example.com:80$/ServerName localhost/' -e 's#^ErrorLog "logs/error_log"$#ErrorLog /proc/self/fd/2#' -e 's#^    CustomLog "logs/access_log" common$#    CustomLog /proc/self/fd/1 common#' "$ROOT/opt/httpd/conf/httpd.conf" && for l in 'Listen 8080' 'User httpd' 'Group httpd' 'ServerName localhost' 'ErrorLog /proc/self/fd/2' '    CustomLog /proc/self/fd/1 common'; do grep -qxF "$l" "$ROOT/opt/httpd/conf/httpd.conf" || { echo "httpd.conf: '$l' not set" >&2; exit 1; }; done
